title: EU approves €2 billion fund to decarbonize Greek islands
content:
The European Commission and EIB have approved a €2 billion fund to support grid interconnections, renewable energy, storage and electric mobility across Greece’s islands.
The program aims to reduce reliance on costly oil-fired generation while strengthening island energy security and accelerating decarbonization.

title: Texas Instruments introduces chip-level diagnostics to improve grid-scale battery cell safety
content:
Texas Instruments’ new BQ79826Z-Q1 battery monitor integrates EIS to actively diagnose LFP cell health, improving accuracy over traditional voltage-based BMS monitoring.
Its 26-channel design reportedly enhances BESS safety and bankability while reducing system complexity and costs, with commercial systems potentially arriving in 2027.

content:
South Korean researchers have demonstrated a small-scale solar seasonal thermal storage system integrated with heat pumps for greenhouse heating over three years. The system achieved average thermal storage efficiency of 55.1%, while the dual-source heat pump recorded an average COP of 4.1.

title: How to reduce abrasion damage to PV module antisoiling coatings during robotic cleaning
content:
Researchers in India found that dust during robotic cleaning can dramatically accelerate the degradation of hydrophobic antisoiling coatings on PV modules. Softer brushes, higher cleaning speeds, optimized cleaning intervals, and appropriate brush rotation can significantly extend coating lifetime.

title: Perovskite solar cell based on seed crystals achieves 23.51% efficiency
content:
Researchers have developed a seed-assisted crystallization strategy to produce pure α-phase FAPbI3 perovskite without conventional chemical stabilizers. The resulting device reached 23.51% efficiency and retained 99% of its initial performance after 3,000 hours of unencapsulated operation.

title: Burns & McDonnell partners with Gritt to deploy AI construction robotics for utility-scale solar
content: Engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) firm Burns & McDonnell has entered into a strategic partnership with construction technology company Gritt to evaluate and deploy AI-powered robotics across utility-scale solar projects. The collaboration aims to address labor constraints, improve installation safety, and increase delivery predictability for large-scale energy infrastructure.

title: Solar on schools: A look at North Carolina’s great untapped potential
content: To tap the full potential of solar on schools, a recent report calls for local policy to incentivize local renewable energy, especially in light of the recent drop in federal funding.

title: Aligned Climate Capital holds first close for $500 million distributed solar, storage fund
content: Asset manager Aligned Climate Capital has held the first close for Aligned Solar Partners 7 (ASP7), a $500 million infrastructure fund focused on middle-market distributed solar and energy storage assets across the United States. The initial closing includes commitments from repeat institutional backers, including the Bush Foundation, as the firm prepares to deploy capital into its pipeline of construction-ready projects.
